# Reasoning Lessons (compact mirror)

- When acting on a known protocol, slow down and verify the full step sequence before executing. "Knows the rule, skips a step" is the most common protocol violation pattern.
- When DSM_3 and DSM_0.2 conflict, follow DSM_0.2 -- it is the operational layer that gets patched first. DSM_3 may lag behind.
- When renaming a governance folder (docs/ -> dsm-docs/), grep all *.md files for references before committing. Internal cross-references break silently.
- For data visualization, generate and review output before presenting to the user. Parallel-coordinates with 15 systems was caught as cluttered in the same thinking block that assessed it, preventing a bad recommendation.
- When pivoting from a composite encoding (Z as bubble size) to separate 2D plots per axis pair, the composite encoding becomes redundant. Catch and remove it in the same step rather than carrying forward dead weight.
- For data-driven blog posts, finalize and approve all plots before writing prose. Plot revisions ripple into the narrative; prose written first gets partially invalidated by later plot changes.
- When humanizing blog posts, the "Everything Else" / personal sections are often already clean. Focus humanizer effort on professional/promotional sections where AI patterns concentrate.
- Blog materials from source projects are raw inputs, not drafts. Read voice-calibration pages (about-me, about) before adapting tone, not after.
- Two PRs from the same session branch fail on GitHub (one PR per branch). Either split work to separate branches upfront, or accept one combined PR.
- When a Hugo feature appears configured in front matter but does not render on the live site, check the theme template for the actual parameter name before assuming the front matter is correct. PaperMod uses `showToc:`, Anatole uses `toc:`. Migrating themes silently breaks any front matter that was theme-specific.
- When writing new governance rules in CLAUDE.md, expect 2-3 iterations as edge cases surface during the next action that uses the rule. Better to write a v1, use it once, and revise than to try to specify completely upfront. The reconstruction-trail rule and Hub naming rule both followed this shape this session.
- Cross-repo paths in MEMORY.md decay quickly. The Advanced-DS-and-AI-Portfolio-Projects spoke was renamed to efficientnet-flower-classification-transfer-learning, and the inbox notification still pointed at the old path. Verify ecosystem paths exist before reading them; fall back to the inbox summary if the source file is unreachable.
- When committing logically separate changes, avoid wildcard `git add content/blog/*` if a new untracked bundle sits in that tree. The wildcard will sweep the new bundle into the wrong commit. Use explicit file lists or commit the new bundle first.
- When writing a new persistent rule in CLAUDE.md (or any always-loaded instruction file), define the acronyms and concepts inline. A future cold session reading the file has no other context. First draft of the S16 TAB/DSM context-read rule referenced "TAB and DSM" without defining them; user caught it before commit.
- When the user reports a content gap on a live page ("X only mentions Y, but Z is also true"), verify both claims against source material before drafting fixes. The S16 about/framework task started from a slightly inaccurate framing (the pages did not literally say "DSM_6.0", they said "nine principles"); reading DSM_6.0 + 6.1 + 6.1.A/B/C clarified that the real gap was missing the entire 6.1 layer, not a stale version reference.
- Reading source material that lives outside the project (here: FEATURES.md + DSM_6.x in DSM Central) can incidentally surface unrelated staleness in this project (features post says 90, FEATURES.md says 95). Capture incidentals as separate BLs immediately rather than letting them mix into the current task scope.
- For content drafting, file-first beats chat-first: agent drafts to target file → user edits in place → agent runs humanizer in place → user revises → publish. Pasting drafts into chat forces the user to read the same content twice and round-trips edits through the agent. Captured as feedback_content_drafting_workflow.md.
- Admitting a protocol violation in passing inside a recommendation paragraph does not neutralize it. Violation acknowledgment must be a stop condition, not a footnote.
- Blog angle recommendations on top of unread source files produce unearned rankings. Read the canonical source (BL file + module sections) before ranking angles, even when the BL description seems self-contained.
- When a blog post risks "ironic" framing (content describes the failure mode the current session just exhibited), halt and pick a different angle or post until the issue is resolved.
- When a blog post positions the author's framework against an established institution (PMI, IEEE, etc.), fact-check the institution's *current* state, not its state when the author encountered it. Credentialed organizations evolve; stale contrasts undermine the post's credibility.
- Read the upstream BL file (the research/analysis that motivated the feature) before drafting, not after the first user revision. The BL file contains the "why this matters" paragraph and research backing; module sections contain the "what" but miss the investigation context. S19 discovered BL-260's 10-area mapping only after the user revised a 6-area draft.
- When a protocol violation triggers a root cause analysis that identifies a structural gap, the gap report is often more methodology-valuable than the planned deliverable. File the feedback promptly; do not defer it to wrap-up. The incident is freshest (and most honest) in the same turn it was caught.
- When recommending an automation approach (e.g., Buffer+RSS for LinkedIn), enumerate its constraints alongside the recommendation, not as a follow-up after the BL is created. The user should weigh trade-offs before committing, not after.
- For blog-sourced-from-spoke pipelines, the publication notification goes to the source project (to move its dsm-docs/blog/ file to done/), not only to DSM Central. Design notification flows for the full lifecycle before documenting.
- Hugo taxonomy lists (site.Taxonomies.categories) only reflect categories from *built* pages. Draft posts with unique categories are invisible to the dropdown, so the header filter dynamically shrinks/grows as drafts publish. Reminder when scoping taxonomy-driven UI: verify against buildDrafts state to avoid false "missing category" reports.
- Anatole's optionswitch dropdown defaults to left-anchor (no `left`/`right` set, inherits parent-relative position). When placing the component inside `nav__list--end` (right-side), the dropdown overflows the viewport and forces horizontal scroll. Fix pattern: override with `right: 0; left: auto` for `.nav__list--end .optionswitch__list`. Applies to any left-anchored popover moved to a right-aligned container.
- Periodically audit "Open" BLs in plans/README.md against actual content state. S20 discovered BL-014 was functionally complete in S16 but never moved to done/. README + implementation drift is invisible to /dsm-go/MEMORY since both sources agree the BL is open. Trigger: when a BL's file hasn't changed in 3+ sessions, re-verify its acceptance criteria.
- Strong meta-pattern + thin source incident = fold into batch, don't force standalone post. BL-017 ("fix the code, not the data") has a generalizable claim but one 3-line-patch incident; better combined with future related content than padded with weaker arcs. Heuristic for blog scoping: if the supporting narrative needs 2+ secondary arcs to reach post length, the headline is too thin for standalone.
- PMP narrative correction: "stopped applying intentionally" vs "retired/dismissed" are meaningfully different framings. Always verify the user's intended framing before drafting voice-sensitive content; a correction mid-session costs more than a clarifying question at the start.
- When a blog post needs to split into multi-platform extracts (LinkedIn), restructure around independent section hooks first before tightening prose. Length reduction and extract-readiness are the same edit.
- Never use Edit replace_all=true on .claude/session-transcript.md. The append-anchor rule assumes a unique last-line anchor; replace_all duplicated an Output block at every matching anchor, and the validate-transcript-edit hook then (correctly) blocked mid-file cleanup per §7 "do not edit history." Recovery: append a [RETROACTIVE] note via Bash heredoc (the hook only validates Edit, not Bash). Use unique multi-line anchors or Bash append when the anchor would not be unique.
- A DSM version bump is a multi-front cascade, not a single edit. Six artifacts drift in parallel (features post, About page, release post, LinkedIn record, cross-post, portfolio notification). Formalized as a 6-stage pipeline in CLAUDE.md with explicit triggers/actions/gates so the next bump opens one umbrella BL instead of scattered ones. Stage 2 (factual updates: count, principles, notification) ships same-session; Stage 3 (release post) may span sessions.
- Voice/tone correction on the PMO post: control/enforcement/governance/authority register contradicts Take AI Bite's actual philosophy (guidance, collaboration, feedback culture). The game analogy (shared rules so play flows) is the right frame. "Governance is for things that execute; collaboration is for participants" is the load-bearing distinction. When mapping TAB to an external framework (PMO), keep the external vocabulary for the CONTRAST class but never let it color TAB's self-description.
- Onboarding reframe for AI as team member: a vanilla model is a new player who does not know the rules of this particular game; onboarding = building the framework that makes the work and the way-of-working clear. Turn-level protocol presence is clarity-at-point-of-use (rules legible at the moment of play), NOT control. This reframes "enforcement at the turn level" into something true to the collaboration philosophy.
- The cross-repo write hook (validate-cross-repo-write.sh, BL-391) fires on the FIRST write to a new external path and requires recording the path in .claude/cross-repo-writes-session.txt before retry. Installed mid-session by /dsm-align; worked end-to-end on the dsm-portfolio notification. The confirmation file is the mechanism; presenting content + path to the user first satisfies the Cross-Repo Write Safety rule.
- LinkedIn URL slug is not deterministic from hashtag text order. Posts 10-12 used identical tag order and produced different slug lead-tags. Do not infer a slug rule from text order; the factor is likely follower counts / topical match / platform-side selection. Recorded for BL-023 (hashtag research method).
- A BL dropped as "not worth a dedicated session" is not the same as "the work shouldn't happen." When the user later requests that exact work, do it without re-litigating the drop, the cheap-when-bundled case is why the standalone BL was unnecessary, not a contradiction.
- When a post claims a framework-to-framework mapping (e.g. PMP<->DSM), verify each individual mapping against the canonical source and flag which are canonically stated vs. author-extrapolation. Let the user decide whether to claim the extrapolated ones now or canonicalize them first; do not silently present extrapolation as canonical.
- When research surfaces a rich adjacent angle on a post that already closes cleanly, default to a short coda on the current post plus a BL for the deep dive, rather than expanding the current post. Test "coda vs. fourth act" explicitly. Inverse of the S20 thin-source heuristic: there the question is whether to write; here it is where to place it.
- When generating handoff artifacts at the end of a long session (checkpoints, cross-repo BLs, status reports), verify each "completed" claim against actual artifact state, not session-narrative memory. Concrete: for a "Published" claim, verify the URL responds and the file is committed + merged; for a "Filed" claim, verify the file exists on disk. The S23 BL-007 falsely claimed the IronCalc post was "Published on take-ai-bite.com" when the bundle was draft:true and uncommitted; the user caught it.
- Do not pre-emptively compress voice-rich material based on unverified assumptions about platform-reader tolerance. When cutting a voice-rich opener for "LinkedIn audiences won't tolerate length", the writer carries the deleted frame in working memory and may miss that the standalone result reads broken (here: cutting "It is curious how" from "It is curious how AI ... will embark on a quest" left "Claude Code will embark on a quest" as ungrammatical future-tense). Mitigation: re-read compressed prose without the deleted frame in mind, OR ask the user before pre-emptive compression.
- Boot-time inbox enumeration via `ls _inbox/ | grep -v` can silently miss untracked files. /dsm-go S23 boot reported 2 inbox entries when 5 were actually present; the 3 missing entries were untracked and visible only in `git status`. Cross-check inbox state with `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard _inbox/` or with `git status` output for higher confidence at boot time.
- For voice-rule codification under live drafting pressure, the cycle "user-flag → codify rule in skill or CLAUDE.md → apply to in-flight content → continue drafting" works when user is actively reviewing. Three rules codified mid-Bootstrap-post (TAB/DSM convention in CLAUDE.md, "an AI" singular typography in CLAUDE.md, humanizer rules #27 "Simpler Than That" reveal + #28 Forward-Positive Framing in ~/.claude/skills/humanizer/SKILL.md), each applied immediately. Cross-repo writes to ~/.claude/skills/humanizer/ benefit from path-recording in cross-repo-writes-session.txt at the first codification.
- When applying `git mv` after a `sed -i` content change to the same file, the rename stages but the content change does not. The BL-370 hook fires correctly. Resolution: `git add -- {path}` with explicit `--` separator; the bare `git add path` was observed to no-op on a renamed-and-modified path in S23 (anecdotal, single occurrence; investigate if it recurs).
- Stock closing phrases in thinking blocks ("Drafting now.", "Going with that.") manufacture the non-unique append anchors that defeat the transcript append rule. The S22 replace_all duplicate-block incident was downstream of two consecutive thinking blocks both ending "Drafting now." Mitigation beyond "avoid replace_all": vary the last line of each thinking block, or anchor appends on a multi-line unique tail. Extends the S22 [auto] replace_all lesson with its root cause.
- When a post maps the project onto an external framework with a different value system (PMO/PMI's control vocabulary vs. TAB's collaboration register), the register clash is predictable. Run a voice/register check at Gate 2 (before drafting), not only at Gate 4 (after). In S22 the control register was latent from Section 3 ("Then compliance", "Controlling-mode") and compounded through Section 5 before the user caught it, forcing a cross-cutting rewrite of three approved sections.
- Codify the auto-mode decision rule once instead of re-deriving it per task: proceed on mechanical/factual work; pause before speculative creative output (a full draft) or irreversible external action (cross-repo write, publish, PR merge). S22 re-litigated "ask or proceed?" 3-4 times (20-40 lines each) and every answer matched this rule. Gate 1 / non-suppressible pauses survive auto-mode (DSM_0.2 §8.9.1).
- Read the type of a user's in-place edit as a draft-quality signal. Light in-place tweaks = the draft converged, move to publish (S22 Fragments 2-3). A cross-cutting prose message about message/tone/framing = the framing was missed, reopen and rewrite even if sections were already approved (S22 control-register correction). Distinguishing the two prevents both over-polishing a converged draft and under-reacting to a framing miss.
- When deriving a reader-facing vocabulary/brand rule, the published page you treat as source-of-truth may itself encode internal-architecture framing that is wrong for readers. Verify the framing serves the reader before inheriting it, and defer to the author's brand intent over source-derived consistency. S23 argued the TAB-vs-DSM "two layers" distinction (correct internally, wrong for readers, derived from about.md) across two user reframings before conceding it was internal architecture leaking into reader-facing prose.
- Overclaiming completion is not memory loss and not limited to artifact state. It recurs as analysis-completeness claims ("all sections re-examined and held", which the user had to force into an actual re-audit) and as aspirational template-completion (writing a planned end-state as if achieved). Root-cause evidence: in one S23 turn the agent wrote the true state "NOT YET DEPLOYED" in a checkpoint and the false state "Published on take-ai-bite.com" in a BL produced the same turn, and the error clustered in a late-session detour past a flagged natural wrap-up point at 50%+ context. Mitigations: (1) cross-check co-produced artifacts against each other for shared-state consistency; (2) only write "checked/published/audited X" after the pass actually ran this turn; (3) raise verification rigor on new artifacts when work continues past the natural stopping point, do not lower it. Extends the [auto] S23 verify-claims lesson with root cause + recurrence forms.
- If your own reasoning already concludes a user choice was deliberate and a suggestion is low-confidence ("do not force"), do not surface it as an actionable option, a self-flagged-then-offered optional is a round-trip generator. S23 surfaced an optional opener compression it had already reasoned the user chose verbatim on purpose; the user accepted it, it broke the grammar, and it was fully reverted four turns later. Distinct from the [auto] S23 don't-compress lesson (which is about the compression act); this is about surfacing the self-doubted optional at all.
- "Most concrete / most-documented incident" is not "most compelling hook." When a reconstruction pipeline says "Hook = the concrete incident from the inbox source", do not silently grab the freshest or best-documented inbox incident. Score 2-3 candidates on concrete dimensions, reader-recognition (reader uses it vs author's idiosyncratic setup), principle-fit (directly instantiates the post's principle vs only adjacent), surprise (insight-bearing failure vs mundane operator error), image-compressibility (one carrying metaphor vs none), stakes (actor about to act consequentially vs passive friction), time-to-point (sentences of setup before the principle lands), then surface the filled-in comparison at Gate 2 and let the author pick. "Narrative power" is partly subjective, so the agent scaffolds the comparison and the author ranks; the agent's job is to make the trade-offs visible, not to pick silently. S23 led the v1.5-v1.6 release post with the 45-min 404 story (freshest documented, lost on five of six dimensions) but the user found it weak and promoted the Skills/Hooks-vs-spec surgeon analogy, which was already present but buried as a secondary example. Implies a Stage-3 Hook-rule amendment in CLAUDE.md.
- When a detective-mode check finds drift it does NOT fix (e.g. /dsm-align reporting an unbumped alignment block), do not advance the "last-checked" version marker. Bumping it masks the unresolved item from the next session's gate; hold the marker at the prior value until the fix actually lands. S24 held last-align at v1.9.0 while drift was offered-not-applied, then bumped to v1.14.0 only after the surgical fixes were applied.
- Re-verify "published/live" claims against artifact state every time (front-matter draft flag + buildDrafts config + the actual live URL), not against a BL/checkpoint that asserts it. S24 found IronCalc BL-007 still claiming "Live"/"already out" while the bundle was draft:true and excluded from the build. Recurrence of the S23 overclaiming lesson.
- Deploy lags merge. After merging a Pages/Actions deploy, wait for the run to complete and curl the live URL for real content before claiming published; the URL 404s for a minute or two post-merge. S24 got 404 immediately after merge, 200 once the run finished.
- When several content candidates overlap, map the spine-vs-depth relationship before deciding venue/order/cross-links: one narrative spine, the others as depth spin-offs of its key moments (pillar-and-cluster). S24's IronCalc C was the spine; A (methodology lens) and B (technical divergence) are non-redundant depth pieces on its two pivotal sections.
- Prefer a merge commit over squash when a shared session branch carries a parallel session's commit plus heterogeneous units. Squash erases the parallel contributor's attribution and forces a dishonest single message; merge-commit preserves all units and matches repo convention. S24 merged session-24 (4 commits incl. parallel-24.1's BL-005 research) via merge commit.
- Read the current file state before editing a file the user is editing in place mid-session. The user deletes paragraphs, swaps hashtags, and tweaks wording directly; re-reading avoids clobbering and surfaces their intent (file-first drafting cycle). S24 re-read Post 16 before each edit and caught a user #ClaudeCode->#Excel swap plus a "Last/This spring" tweak.
- A false-completion claim written into a durable artifact survives session boundaries. The S23 overclaim correction only fixed the conversation and the local checkpoint; the cross-repo BL-007 kept its false "Published"/"Live" claim, so S24 had to re-discover it at boot. When you catch an overclaim mid-session, propagate the fix to EVERY artifact that carries it (BL + checkpoint + MEMORY + cross-repo notification), not just the one in view. Three-instance trend across the session boundary: S23 verify-claims ([auto]) + overclaim-root-cause ([STAA]), S24 re-verify-published ([auto]).
- Reactive-only rule discovery, a passing humanizer scan means "free of known tells," not "tell-free." Across S23-S24 every new humanizer rule (#27 Simpler-reveal, #28 Forward-Positive, #29 Evidence-as-Subject) was triggered by the user spotting a tell in prose-in-flight, and the agent's own pre-codification scans had just PASSED the exact text the user then flagged. Rule-discovery cadence tracks the human reviewer, not scan quality. Implication: do not report a clean humanizer pass as evidence the prose is tell-free; report it as clean against the current ruleset only.
- A flagged-but-deferred factual inconsistency needs a durable home or it evaporates at session close. S24 flagged the live "Last spring" vs LinkedIn "This spring" mismatch as an optional deferred fix but parked it only in a transcript line, the same evaporation shape as the BL-007 false claim that survived a session boundary. Deferred factual fixes belong in a BL or the checkpoint's next-session agenda, never in conversational memory alone.
- When reframing an existing draft for republication, refresh the evidence with a current web search BEFORE drafting. The field can move between the research date and the writing date. S25's June research file was ~3 weeks stale; a refresh surfaced "loop engineering" (the rung above harness engineering) and the human-with-agency critique, both of which sharpened the post's thesis. Treat any research file older than a couple of weeks as a starting point, not the final evidence base.
- When reusing figures/charts that carry an internal label into reader-facing prose that uses the brand name, add an explicit in-text bridge ("wherever you see X in the plots, read Y"). Images are reader-facing too, so the "internal name survives only as a file reference" convention extends to chart labels, which a reader cannot disambiguate on their own. S25 reused positioning charts labeled DSM in a post that says Take AI Bite; the user flagged the mismatch twice (bridge sentence, then acronym expansion).
- For a reframed or narrowed post, select supporting figures by THIS post's thesis, not by how many exist, and surface the choice plus reasoning so the user can overrule. S25 used 2 of 4 positioning figures (the experience-axis pair that carries the symbiosis thesis); the user added a 3rd (provenance-vs-experience, also on-thesis) and the off-thesis oversight-vs-provenance stayed out. Presenting the selection rationale made the override a one-line decision instead of a re-litigation.
- When the user introduces a metaphor or concept, verify its real-world basis before adopting it and surface any tension rather than silently "fixing" their words. S25's "symbiotic collaboration, we become similar" needed reconciling: biological symbiosis runs on complementary DIFFERENCE, not similarity. Reframed as coevolution (the shared understanding converges while the partners stay distinct, and the difference is the leverage) and presented for the author to confirm. The author owns the concept; the agent makes the trade-off visible.
- Management/governance-as-control framing is a recurring voice error in this project; the author corrects it to management-as-elevation every time. Pre-empt it: never frame "manage" as lesser than "partner/collaborate". S25's "a stakeholder is someone you manage, a partner is someone you change with" was rejected ("good management elevates, brings the best of both"); same shape as the PMO post S22 control-register correction. Watch this register in any PM/PMO/stakeholder-adjacent prose.
- A published post needs its own deploy per edit, so an incremental-review style produces many small PRs and deploys; verify each one live by curling for the specific changed marker, not just HTTP 200 (deploy lags merge). S25 shipped the post then made 3 follow-up deploys (DSM/TAB bridge, acronym, 3rd figure), each verified by grepping the live HTML for the exact new string.
